title: Lack of skilled manpower impedes progress of animation, gaming
publisher: The Economic Times / Press Trust of India, reporting a NASSCOM report release
methodology: The article reports NASSCOM's estimate for approximately 150 gaming companies but gives no sampling frame, collection date, worker-status definition, contractor treatment or original report title. It separately reports a combined animation-and-gaming total of 16,500 for 2006; that broader number is not proposed as a game-employment observation.
assessment: Useable only as an explicitly secondary, association-attributed historical game-company stock. The 2,500 value is dated and scope-distinct, but its original NASSCOM edition was not located. It cannot be made comparable with later online-gaming or broad-sector estimates.
access_status: full public article inspected; exact text available in page readback
next_step: Locate the 2007 NASSCOM Animation and Gaming report or release archive before upgrading this observation's provenance. Do not use the 13,000 2010 forecast as an observation.

title: TeamLease Digital reports index: Gaming: Tomorrow's Blockbuster
methodology: The publisher index identifies the report and says it covers gaming-industry growth, job opportunities, hiring and skilling. It does not expose the downloadable report text, its sampling frame or its employment-estimation methodology in the public page inspected.
assessment: Authoritative publisher-level edition and date evidence for the source used by subsequent EY work, but not sufficient by itself to reproduce the 50,000 claim.
access_status: public report index inspected; report download is premium/gated in the visible index
next_step: Obtain the original November 2022 PDF or a TeamLease release archive to recover its research method and whether 'directly employs' excludes contractors and RMG support roles.

title: Game to Gain - Gaming industry to add 1 lakh new jobs by FY23 - states TeamLease Digital
publisher: CXOtoday reproducing TeamLease Digital's 17 November 2022 release
years: 2022 current direct-employment estimate; FY23 forecasts excluded
methodology: The release says TeamLease Digital's report is a deep dive on growth and hiring/skilling sentiment. It states that the sector directly employed about 50,000 people and describes roles, but it gives no respondent count, company frame, data-collection dates or calculation method.
assessment: Best accessible source-native release text for the 50,000 current direct-employment figure. It is a broad gaming-sector stock and not a core-development census; retain separately and exclude the stated 100,000 new-jobs forecast.
next_step: Use the TeamLease original report if recovered; otherwise retain 50,000 with the reproduced-release qualifier.

title: New frontiers: Navigating the evolving landscape for online gaming in India
methodology: The report calls the 100,000 figure an approximately current total across direct and indirect core and support roles and cites TeamLease Digital Gaming Report November 2022. Its factsheet labels 100,000 employees and 15,000 game developers/programmers as FY23. The report does not publish the TeamLease population frame, survey, multiplier or a separate derivation for 15,000.
assessment: Decisive dated source for a broad FY23 online-gaming employment stock and a narrow occupational subset, with substantial scope limitations. It states RMG was 82.8% of FY23 online-gaming market value, so neither measure is eligible as a core video-game-development comparison. It resolves the baseline's undated 66,000/130,000 problem only by adding a separate, transparently broad series.
access_status: full public PDF downloaded to raw/ey-online-gaming-2023.pdf and text-extracted to raw/ey-online-gaming-2023.txt
next_step: Recover TeamLease's November 2022 report method before treating the FY23 100,000 figure as more than a publisher-attributed broad estimate. Search later EY/FICCI editions for a dated replacement only if they state the reference year and scope.

title: NASSCOM Gaming Forum in association with App Annie and Deloitte releases white papers
methodology: The accessible search extract describes NASSCOM Gaming Forum and the Applied Games in India report but gives no game-industry employment stock; the PDF itself returned 406 to this research route.
assessment: Negative result. The later NASSCOM gaming source located in this bounded sweep provides market/association context, not a dated workforce count.
access_status: search-index text inspected; direct PDF access rejected with HTTP 406
next_step: Do not infer employment from NASSCOM's all-IT workforce or membership figures. Recover older 2007 source before adding any other NASSCOM employment observation.
